tells: Brand-name cosplay: 'allegrolokalnie' is wearing the real company's name like a borrowed suit, parked up front where a phone screen will show it and then politely give up.

Read the address right to left, like a skeptic. The part that actually owns the page is 'aukcja758487593.top', which is a lottery ticket number on a domain ending that costs about as much as a gas station hot dog.
'/logowanie/48819' means 'login' in Polish plus a listing number, the URL equivalent of a fake mustache: technically a disguise, mostly a confession.
items.critic_note: Putting 'allegrolokalnie' in front of 'aukcja758487593.top' is the web equivalent of taping a Gucci logo to a cardboard box. The whole con depends on your phone cutting the address off after the first word, which, to be fair, it will. Ours did.

tells: Five buzzwords walked into a subdomain ('walletsupport-ledger-live-login-ch') and none of them were hired by Ledger. Real companies don't need to shout every keyword at once to prove who they are.
The real owner of this address is 'vercel.app', a free hosting service anyone can sign up for in two minutes. That's like Rolex running its flagship store out of a borrowed folding table.

Ledger Live is an app on your own device. It has never needed you to 'log in' on a website, and no real support person will ever ask for your 24-word recovery phrase. Anyone who does isn't support; they're the robbery.
items.critic_note: Nothing says 'official hardware security' like a 34-character hyphen salad on a free hobbyist hosting plan. If a domain has more dashes than a Morse code message, keep walking. Then run.

rejected_log.reason: Human review caught '_phishme.com_session_id' cookie in scan metadata — likely a corporate phishing simulation/training domain, not a criminal knockoff. Excluded from the main aisle.
